Nathamunigal is considered to be the second guru of the Sri Vaishnava Guru Parampara. He is believed to have been born near Viranarayanapuram, near modern-day Mannargudi, in what is believed to be 823 AD. He is credited with the resurgence and the compilation of the Naalayira Divyaprabandhangal.
 
At one point, all of the Naalayira Divyaprabandhangal were lost except for ten pashurams that were being sung at this temple. Here, Naathamunigal heard this, and the verses told ten out of a thousand pashurams. This had Naathamunigal intrigued as to where the other nine hundred and ninety pashurams had disappeared. These ten pashurams also spoke of Kurugur (present-day Azhwar Tirunagari), Sadagopan (Nammazhwar). Thus Naathamunigal went in search of Nammazhwar. Upon reaching Kurugur and enquiring about these ten pashurams, the locals denied knowing of the ten pashurams that he asked for, but they knew of eleven other pashurams. Naathamunigal recited these eleven pashurams twelve thousand times in front of the divine tamarind tree where Nammazhwar had once resided. Upon completion of the recitation, Nammazhwar is said to have appeared in front of Naathamunigal and blessed him with the thousand pashurams sung by him, as well as the three thousand other pashurams which were sung by the nine other azhwars. Nathamunigal is said to have taught the Naalayira Divyaprabandhangal to his two nephews at Srirangam and introduced them at the Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple, where he served as the temple administrator.
The ritual of worship, as followed in Vishnu Temples, is based on two early standard works. The first is the Vaikhanasa Sutra, which probably belongs to the Krishna Yajurveda school. The other is the Panchratra Agama, which belongs to the extensive Tantra literature, believed to have been composed by Lord Sriman Narayana himself. The Agama has a peculiar philosophy of its own, the Bhagavata Cult, which is very old and is referred to in the Mahabharata and Badarayana Sutras. Nathamunigal made a provision for the recitation of Tamil Vedas on appropriate occasions during the main festivals of the Lord.
Nathamunigal is said to have attained Paramapadam at Gangaikona Cholapuram.
Nathamunigal's grandson, Yamunacharya, became the torch-bearer of Sri Vaishnava Philosophy.
